clue.text: Homeless woman happy to sit in tree

indicators.note: the word for happy is placed so that it sits inside the word for the tree

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree
glad means happy

explanation.surface: A woman with no home is content to perch up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sit in' is the container signal; 'happy' is not the definition, which is the homeless woman at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag lady is a destitute woman who carries her possessions around in carrier bags and sleeps rough.

clue.text: Villain's unusually coloured hair

parts.note: blue is an unusual colour for a person's facial hair
a beard is hair on the chin

explanation.surface: The bad guy is recognisable by his oddly tinted locks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In the folk tale, the wife-murdering nobleman with a blue beard is a byword for a murderous husband.

clue.text: Country's oil reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken out loud, so the word for oil is heard rather than seen

parts.note: grease is oil or lubricant

explanation.surface: A nation's petroleum output appears in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a nation in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Wanting 100% acquisition, in spite of everything

parts.note: to be after something is to want it or seek it
100% of something is all of it

explanation.surface: Someone greedy wants to take over completely, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquisition' fills out the reading: someone after all is seeking to acquire the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning nevertheless, despite what has happened or been said.

clue.text: Law limiting those who can succeed at the highest level

definitions.text: Law limiting those who can succeed at the highest level

parts.words: Law limiting those who can succeed at the highest level
parts.note: read not as a rule about career success but as a statute restricting who may inherit the crown

explanation.surface: A rule that caps who gets to reach the top of their profession.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1701 Act of Settlement limits succession to the British throne to Protestant heirs of Sophia of Hanover; 'succeed' means inherit, and 'the highest level' is the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1701 statute settled the royal succession, barring Catholics from the British throne.

clue.text: Important people including some copper?

definitions.meaning: senior officers or high-ranking figures in an organisation
a jokey literal reading: the best brass, an alloy that contains copper

explanation.surface: VIPs, perhaps one of whom is a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman among the bigwigs, but it is the metal: brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is an idiom for the highest-ranking officers or executives; brass itself is an alloy made with copper.

clue.text: Half of Spanish football team leaving the field

indicators.note: only the first five of the ten letters of the club's name are kept

parts.note: Real Madrid is the famous Spanish football club

explanation.surface: Part of a Spanish football side walks off the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' joins the wordplay to the definition. 'field' looks like the football pitch but means an area of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or sphere of activity or interest.

clue.text: Queen wearing sort of fabric right for shiny coat

indicators.note: the queen is dressed in the other letters, so she goes inside them

parts.note: lace is a kind of openwork fabric

explanation.surface: The monarch dresses in lace, which suits a glossy finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' is the container signal: the queen is clothed by the fabric plus right. 'coat' is a layer of finish, not a garment; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a varnish that dries to a hard glossy finish.

clue.text: Female to go the other side of the channel, one suffering accident

parts.words: to go the other side of the channel
parts.note: across the English Channel, in France, the verb to go is aller

explanation.surface: A woman crosses the Channel and has a mishap on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other side of the channel' signals a French word: aller is French for 'to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A faller is a person or horse that takes a fall, as in a steeplechase.

clue.text: End act swirling round a piano — entertaining performance

indicators.note: the swirled letters go around the next two pieces
the letters of end act are whirled into a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A dancer spins about a grand piano to finish the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges END ACT into TDANCE, and 'round' puts it around A and P (piano), giving T-AP-DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dancing is a stage routine where rhythm is beaten out with metal-tipped shoes.

clue.text: Intimate pal to change and say nothing

parts.note: to alter is to change
say means for example, abbreviated e.g.
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A close friend who switches sides and keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say nothing' looks like keeping silent but splits as EG (say, for example) and O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a very close and trusted friend, literally a second self.

clue.text: Odd sixty minutes when husband escapes for gossip

parts.note: rum is an informal British word for odd or strange

indicators.note: the letter for husband gets away from the word for an hour

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour

explanation.surface: A strange hour while the husband slips out gives rise to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escapes' removes H from HOUR, leaving OUR; 'when' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour is unconfirmed talk or hearsay passed between people.

clue.text: Lying down doing nothing with lids seen getting tight

indicators.note: someone getting tight is getting drunk, so the letters of lids seen reel about

explanation.surface: A drowsy person lies still, eyelids clenching shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' means drunk, the anagram signal; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is inactivity, the state of lazing about with no work.

clue.text: English stories about evil prince's home

indicators.note: the word for stories goes around the word for evil

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional stories
sin is wickedness, evil

explanation.surface: English tales surround the wickedness at a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The prince is Hamlet, Prince of Denmark, whose castle home gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the Danish castle where Shakespeare sets Hamlet, the prince's residence.

clue.text: Inert, suffering with acne? Get fruit!

indicators.note: the letters are in distress and twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Lethargic and spotty? Eat some fruit!
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges INERT with ACNE; 'with' and 'Get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach.

clue.text: Eight for dinner maybe?

parts.note: eight is read not as a number of guests but as eight o'clock, an hour when people sit down to eat

explanation.surface: Perhaps eight guests are coming to dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight o'clock might be the hour at which a meal is served.

clue.text: Rigorous examination that involves litmus paper?

definitions.meaning: a decisive trial of worth or quality
read literally, a chemistry check of whether something is acidic

explanation.surface: A demanding exam involving litmus paper in the lab.
explanation.walkthrough: Litmus paper turns red in acid, so the phrase can be read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a decisive trial comes from the use of nitric acid to tell gold from base metals.

clue.text: Bishop's robe has a fire-spouting monster

parts.note: a chimer is a sleeveless robe worn by Anglican bishops

explanation.surface: A bishop's vestment features a dragon breathing flames.
explanation.walkthrough: The chimer (or chimere) is the bishop's sleeveless outer robe; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Chimera was a fire-breathing beast with lion, goat and serpent parts.

clue.text: It's a nuisance collecting rubbish — object

indicators.note: the word for a nuisance gathers up the word for rubbish inside it

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person or thing
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Picking up litter is a chore, someone complains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' is the container signal. 'object' is the verb, to raise an objection, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to raise an objection against something.

clue.text: Like far-reaching plans that may tire students out

definitions.meaning: describing schemes that cover an extended future period
read literally, an extended school term that exhausts pupils

explanation.surface: Ambitious strategies that could exhaust the student body.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a term is a school or university teaching period.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-term plans look well into the future; a lengthy term of study could wear pupils out.

clue.text: Having drunk rum, man made a mistake

indicators.note: the man takes the next word inside him, as if he had swallowed it

parts.note: Ned is a man's name
rum here is the British slang adjective meaning odd

explanation.surface: After downing some rum, a fellow slipped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' wants to be the drink but is the adjective meaning strange; 'Having drunk' is the container signal. The saying 'even Homer nods' means even the best make mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod is to slip up through a lapse of attention, as in 'Homer sometimes nods'.

clue.text: Get rid of little girl with short magical formula

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its final letter

parts.note: a spell is a set of magic words

explanation.surface: A small girl and a quick charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter of SPELL, leaving SPEL; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or banish, such as fears or doubts.

clue.text: Smooth tree

definitions.meaning: to make level, as a woodworker's tool does
a tall broad-leaved tree common in city streets

explanation.definitionFit: A plane is a tool for levelling wood, and also a tree often lining London streets.

clue.text: Friend drinking a river or sober?

indicators.note: the friend takes the river inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend
the Oder is a river in central Europe

explanation.surface: A pal downs a whole river, or does he stay dry?
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' is the container signal; 'a' and 'or' are links. 'sober' reads as teetotal but means restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate means temperate or restrained, as a sober person is.

clue.text: No image appearing in the photographic process

definitions.meaning: a reply of refusal or denial

definitions.text: image appearing in the photographic process
definitions.meaning: the reversed-tone image on film from which prints are made

explanation.surface: No picture emerges during the developing of a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative is a denial, and in photography the film image with light and dark reversed.

clue.text: Man having hesitation to get home

parts.note: er is the sound made when hesitating
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A fellow who dithers about finding somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' and 'to get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's name, as in the title character of Wilde's play.

clue.text: Ben's mate relocated in garden flat?

indicators.note: the letters of Ben's mate are moved to new positions

explanation.surface: Ben's friend has moved into a flat with a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocated' rearranges BENS MATE. A garden flat is a ground-level or below-ground flat opening onto a garden, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the lowest storey of a building, below ground level.
